claims.text: Adaptive bias force or metadynamics can be implemented as the methodological intervention.
Advanced sampling will improve representation of atomic configurations in the ab initio liquid of multicomponent high-entropy alloys near their melting temperatures.
The intervention is applicable to both solid and liquid states at or near high melting temperatures.
The intervention will improve phase-space overlap between the reference and target systems.
Advanced sampling enhances exploration of phase space.
Enhanced phase-space exploration leads to improved representation of atomic configurations.
Advanced sampling will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The thermodynamic-integration path mismatch will be reduced by an estimated 20–50%.
The proposed application range includes equiatomic or near-equiatomic alloys.
The proposed temperature range is near the alloy melting point.
TOR-TILD's EAM references are the comparison baseline.
The exact reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch is uncertain.
The optimal choice between advanced sampling techniques is uncertain.
Free-energy values and phase-space-overlap metrics will be compared against results obtained with TOR-TILD's EAM references.
Failure to reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by at least 10% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references will falsify the hypothesis.
